content: I want to build an app to save and manage bookmarks.

The baseline specification is ready for review: [spec.md](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/spec.md).

It defines a private, account-based bookmark manager with:

- Saving, viewing, editing, favoriting, tagging, and deleting bookmarks
- Search and filtering
- Mobile and desktop support
- Keyboard accessibility
- Duplicate-link prevention
- Clear exclusions for collaboration, browser extensions, imports/exports, folders, and offline use

All specification quality checks passed: [requirements checklist](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/checklists/requirements.md).

Feature directory: `specs/001-bookmark-manager`

No code or implementation plan has been created. Please approve the specification or tell me what you’d like changed. Once approved, I’ll move to the planning gate.

Thanks — I read through it and it's a good start. A lot of it matches what I picture. But before I sign off, there are some things I expected that either aren't here or are deliberately left out, and a few of them really matter to me.

The biggest one: when I save a link, I don't want to have to type the title and description myself every time. I'd expect that if I just paste in a web address, the app goes and grabs the page's name, a short description, and its little icon for me — I can tweak it after, but the point is I shouldn't have to do that work by hand. Right now it reads like I'm required to type the title, and the notes even say pulling that info automatically isn't part of this. That's a miss for me.

A few more things I assumed I'd have:

- A "read it later" idea. Sometimes I save something meaning to get to it, and I'd like to flag those and see just that list, then check them off once I've read them.
- Being able to tuck a bookmark away without deleting it — put it aside so it's out of my normal list, but I can still get it back later. Deleting feels too final for stuff I might still want.
- Sorting my list — at least by name or by when I added it. You've listed sorting as out of scope, but I'd want basic control over the order.
- Search that's a bit smarter than plain word matching — like searching an exact phrase, or combining a couple of tags to narrow things down.

And two I'd at least want us to talk about rather than rule out flat: keeping my own saved copy of a page so I don't lose it if the site disappears, and being able to bring in the bookmarks I already have (and get them back out).

I'm fine leaving out the collaboration, teams, and browser-extension stuff — that's not what I need right now.

Could you fold in the automatic title/description-grabbing, the read-later, the set-aside/archive, sorting, and the smarter search, and let me know your thinking on saved copies and importing? Then I'll be happy to look again.

content:
The revised specification is ready: [spec.md](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/spec.md).

It now includes:

- Automatic title, description, and site-icon retrieval with editable previews and sensible fallbacks
- A read-later queue with read/unread status
- Reversible archive and restore
- Sorting by title or date in either direction
- Exact-phrase search and combined tag/state filters
- Imports from Chrome, Edge, Firefox, and Safari bookmark exports
- Complete export and restoration of app-specific data

My recommendation on saved copies is recorded as a deliberate follow-up feature. Page snapshots are valuable, but they introduce storage limits, privacy, unsafe-content handling, update behavior, and content-rights questions that merit their own specification. They are deferred, not rejected.

The updated [quality checklist](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/checklists/requirements.md) passes with no unresolved clarification markers.

No planning or implementation has started. If you approve this revision, I’ll proceed to the implementation-plan gate.

This looks great — you've picked up everything I raised, and it reads the way I'd actually use it.

Walking through it: pasting a link and having the title, description, and icon come back for me to tweak is exactly what I wanted. The read-later list with marking things read, the set-aside-and-restore for archiving, sorting by name or date, the exact-phrase search and narrowing by more than one tag — all of that matches what I pictured. And being able to bring my existing bookmarks in and get my whole collection back out gives me peace of mind about committing to this.

On saved copies of pages — I'm fine with your plan. You're not throwing it away, just handling it properly on its own later, and the reasons you gave (storage, privacy, what happens when a page changes) make sense to me. I'd like to keep it on the list as a real "next" thing, and I trust it'll come back around.

One small thing I noticed, not a blocker: when I add a tag while organizing a bookmark, I'd hope that as I start typing it suggests tags I've already used, so I don't accidentally make a slightly different duplicate of one I already have. If that's already the intent behind reusing existing tags, great — just wanted to make sure that little as-you-type help is there.

With that noted, I'm happy with this specification. Please go ahead to the planning step.

content:
The implementation plan is ready for review: [plan.md](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/plan.md).

Key decisions include:

- React 19 and Fastify 5 in one TypeScript application
- SQLite with full-text search
- Secure, DNS-pinned metadata retrieval
- Same-origin cookie authentication
- Browser-compatible HTML export plus lossless JSON backups
- Vitest, component tests, and Playwright acceptance testing

Supporting artifacts:

- [Technical research](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/research.md)
- [Data model](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/data-model.md)
- [API contract](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/contracts/openapi.yaml)
- [Backup contract](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/contracts/backup.schema.json)
- [Browser interchange contract](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/contracts/browser-bookmarks.md)
- [Validation guide](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/quickstart.md)

The API contract passes validation, the backup schema is valid JSON, and there are no unresolved technical clarifications. The tag suggestion behavior is explicitly included in the approved [specification](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/spec.md).

That all lines up with what I asked for.

Review login:

- Email: `review@example.com`
- Password: `keepmark-review-2026`

Implemented: automatic page details, editable previews, read later, archive/restore, favorites, tag suggestions, phrase and multi-tag search, sorting, browser imports, browser exports, and complete backup/restore.

Validation passed:

- 99 implementation tasks completed
- 33 unit/integration/component tests
- 5 API contract tests
- 14 desktop/mobile browser scenarios
- Type checking, linting, migrations, and production build

Setup and security documentation is in [README.md](/work/README.md). Saved page copies remain documented as the next separately specified feature.

I took it for a proper spin, and it does what we agreed on. Signing in gets me to my own private collection, and trying to peek without being logged in just gets turned away, which is what I'd want for something private.

The things I cared about all work the way I pictured:

- Pasting a link brings back the page details for me to look over, and when a page can't be reached it still lets me save with a sensible fallback title instead of just failing.
- Trying to save something I already have stops me and points me at the one I've got — even when I typed it in a slightly different way, like different capitalization or an extra slash on the end.
- My read-later list shows only what I haven't gotten to, and checking something off clears it out.
- Setting things aside with archive takes them out of my normal view but keeps them safe, and I can pull them back.
- Marking favorites, filtering down by a couple of tags at once, searching an exact phrase in quotes, and sorting by name or date each way all behave.
- I can pull my whole collection out as both a browser-friendly file and a full backup, and the import is there for bringing things in.
- And the tag suggestions I asked about are there.

Saved copies of pages we already agreed to hold for a later round, so I'm not counting that against this. I'm happy with what you've delivered — this is the bookmark manager I asked for. Consider it accepted.
